title: Adaptive tenant-aware pagination controller with cost/SLA hints
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Console dashboard queries currently use a one-size-fits-all page size and prefetch policy. This leads to avoidable token and CPU costs for low-usage tenants, and occasional tail-latency spikes for high-throughput tenants when aggressive prefetching is applied. We need an adaptive controller that picks pagination parameters per-tenant based on usage history, SLA tier, and an explicit cost budget/hint.

Goals / Proposal:
1) Build an Adaptive Pagination Controller (APC) in the query API runtime that computes per-request pagination parameters (page_size, lookahead_k, async_prefetch) using: historical per-tenant request shape summary, tenant SLA tier, and an optional cost_budget_hint submitted by Console or billing.
2) Add a lightweight telemetry summarizer job (hourly) that emits compact per-tenant access histograms: typical page depth, read frequency, 95/99 latency bands, token-per-page distribution. Stored in the config store as a TTL-cached policy datapoint.
3) Controller must be conservative by default: if no history, fall back to current defaults. Make behavior configurable via feature flags and allow tenant opt-out.
4) Integrate with runtime batching and KV cache: controller will avoid aggressive lookahead when request is served from KV cache to prevent wasted prefetch.
5) Provide a cost-aware mode: given tenant cost_budget_hint (tokens/day or tokens/query), trade off prefetch vs latency (bounded by SLA).

Implementation outline:
- Telemetry summarizer (new service job): aggregates logs/dataset produced by query-proxy and writes compact profiles to config-store with TTL.
- Policy store: per-tenant profile + versioning.
- Runtime controller (inside dashboard query API): pulls profile (with local async cache) and selects params; stable for the life of requestId to avoid jitter.
- Admin controls in Console: toggle APC per-tenant and set a cost_budget_hint.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95% of tenants see equal-or-lower tokens/query after 2 weeks in opt-in canary, with <=5% degradation in p50 latency for heavy tenants.
- No more than 0.5% of queries exceed existing p99 latency baseline attributable to APC after rollout (monitored via traces and tail sampling).
- Feature flag exists and can be toggled per-tenant without service restart.
- Unit + integration tests and a synthetic replay test show controller reduces median tokens/query for low-activity tenants by at least 20%.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Dev + internal QA. Deploy summarizer to staging and enable APC for internal tenants only.
- Phase 1: Canary 5% opt-in tenant cohort (non-critical tenants). Monitor metrics dashboard (see links) for two weeks.
- Phase 2: Expand to 25% with gradual increases and allow manual rollback.
- Phase 3: Optional global default-on for P3/P2 tenants if metrics stable; P0 tenants have explicit opt-in enabled.

Observability / Metrics to add:
- tokens_per_query per-tenant (histogram)
- page_fetch_count per-query and wasted_prefetch_count
- p50/p95/p99 query latency per-tenant
- APC policy cache hit rate and config-store e2e latency
- rollout health (errors, rate-limited decisions)

Security / Compliance: controller touches only aggregated tenant-level profiles (no raw user data). Profiles must be TTLed and access-controlled via existing RBAC.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Incorrect profiles for bursty tenants could cause degraded latency; mitigated by conservative defaults and quick rollback flag.
- Extra config-store reads could add latency; mitigate with local async cache and leaky-bucket refresh.
- Prefetch interplay with batching may reduce batching efficiency; controller prefers batching-friendly parameters for high-concurrency tenants.

Links:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Console/pages/APC-Design-Doc
- Synthetic replay harness (internal): https://go/redwood-replay/apc-harness
